Exhaust eligible work: the mode stops. Add eligible work afterward: it remains stopped until manually enabled again. Every newly started item gets a distinct session with its own work brief, applicable instructions and scoped context; the prior item’s conversation must not become its transcript. Verify this for keep-working, scheduled and manually started work and newly delegated task assignments, preserving source-action/history links. Continue an existing paused item and verify its established history and continuity instead. Inspect mode controls and activity. AGENT 01–02, 10–17; WORK 09–10; CONTEXT 01–06; CONTROL 08–11; JOB 07.

Remove a project from active management through the UI and permitted agent tools: verify the default outcome is archival, with its records and linked work/agent/transcript/Git/review/evidence history retained and accessible through archived browsing. Verify ordinary removal does not trigger permanent deletion. Inspect the separate explicit permanent-deletion action without treating it as the default removal path. Request archival with agents active: warn and require confirmation; decline and verify the project and execution remain unchanged. Confirm while tool/process work is active: immediately block dispatch and interrupt all project work without waiting for a safe step or task completion. Verify project schedules, keep-working and agent-tool paths cannot start archived work, and unrelated projects continue. Preserve recorded history and interrupted state. Do not treat cancellation as proof that an already dispatched external effect was undone; reconcile uncertain outcomes before future execution. Restore the archived project and verify that work, keep-working and project schedules remain stopped until the user explicitly reactivates them; restoration alone must not restart execution or bypass existing pauses, approvals or budgets. Permanent deletion follows the separate harness-only boundary under WORK-17. WORK 01, 03, 07, 15–17; CONTROL 03, 05–07; HISTORY 01–02; ART 01–05.

Explicitly delete a project and verify removal of its harness data and artifacts according to the chosen ownership rules. Verify local repository files, worktrees and branches and GitHub repositories, issues, PRs, branches and other resources remain unchanged. Verify neither UI nor agent-tool deletion invokes Git cleanup or remote mutation. Share an artifact across two projects, delete one, and verify its contents and the remaining project’s access/reference survive. Shared-data ownership and deletion mechanics remain open. WORK 03, 15–17; ART 01–05.

Set, save and reopen the app-wide repository base directory. Verify a project inherits it, set a project override, and verify that project uses its override while other projects still inherit. Clear the override and verify inheritance returns. Under the proposed path behavior, validate unavailable locations, use the default for a new clone, retain repositories elsewhere, and verify changing the base does not move existing repositories or change their recorded paths. SET 01–02, 07–08.

Set the app-wide backend and verify project inheritance, an independent project override, and restoration of inheritance when cleared. Select Docker and Podman on supported targets and Apple container on a supported Mac with prerequisites installed. Exercise the declared operation set through the selected adapter and inspect attributed status/logs. Verify missing or incompatible runtimes do not prevent ordinary harness use, no silent engine substitution occurs, reviewer mutations are denied, and unsupported Compose/API/network/volume capabilities are explicit. Close the app with both agent-work and pre-existing/manually managed containers running: verify only agent-work containers stop and shutdown does not delete images, volumes or stored data. Other lifecycle/recovery details remain open. CONTAINER 01–04; TOOL 01–07; RES 01–03; PLAT 01–03.

Open Help near Settings; search for UI actions, configuration scope, autonomous workflows, recovery and extension development. Follow each screen and Settings-section Help link and verify it opens the relevant local topic. Verify documentation covers implemented behavior and every supported extension point, with usable package/language-pack development examples. Retrieve the same topics through coordinator, worker and reviewer documentation tools, subject to configured permissions; documentation cannot grant writes or override user directions. Validate coverage and freshness against the working product. title: 24 Document knowledge and retrieval
intro: Built-in document retrieval augmented generation is required. Users can add their own knowledge documents, index their content into searchable vectors and retrieve relevant passages through the app and agent tools. This extends the unified Knowledge system; a document corpus is source evidence rather than a separate memory, lesson or claim catalog. Plain SQLite and sqlite-vec are the selected app storage. The details marked Proposed below require review.
blocks: Provide a built-in RAG system for knowledge from documents: ingest document content, generate and store searchable vector representations, and retrieve relevant document passages for agents and human search. Users must be able to add knowledge documents of their own and have those documents indexed. This must not be limited to developer-shipped Help, convention pages, existing code indexes or externally hosted corpora.

Expose a Documents area within the Knowledge workspace, backed by the same document ingestion and retrieval operations available through configured agent tools. Support adding local files using a selection dialog or drag and drop, inspecting source text and indexing status, searching the corpus, opening a result at its source passage, reindexing, disabling and removing a document from active retrieval. Include explicit sharing and Move to project controls under RAG-11. Show title, source, tags, project/shared scope, version, indexed time, chunk counts and errors. Imported documents are managed project artifacts under RAG-12. Removing an index must not silently delete an external original or the retained managed artifact; artifact deletion follows the existing explicit deletion and shared-reference rules. A chat attachment is not automatically a durable corpus document unless explicitly added or covered by a configured ingestion rule.

Use a staged pipeline for supported document formats: extract text and structural locators, normalize it, split it into meaningful bounded chunks, generate embeddings through the internal router, and publish searchable chunks with source provenance. Markdown, plain text, PDF and Word documents are required under RAG-09. Initial Word ingestion supports modern .docx only under RAG-09; native extraction adapters remain to qualify. Routed vision fallback for scanned pages is confirmed under RAG-10. Report unsupported or encrypted sources and failed extraction honestly rather than marking empty content successfully indexed. Folder watching, remote URL ingestion and additional formats remain open choices; no mandatory preinstalled Node, Python or office runtime may be introduced into core use.

Support user-added Markdown, plain text, PDF and Word documents for knowledge ingestion, indexing and retrieval. These four document formats are required initial capabilities, not optional future formats. Apply the same indexing visibility, source provenance, project scope and agent retrieval requirements to each. Initial Word support is modern .docx only; legacy binary .doc is excluded from initial support. Scanned or image-only pages use the configurable routed vision fallback under RAG-10. Do not silently report failed or empty extraction as successful indexing.

Extract existing document text directly where available, and use a configured vision-capable model through the internal router as the fallback for scanned or image-only pages. Enable this vision extraction fallback by default. Expose the fallback and its model/route configuration in Settings, with enable/disable control. This pathway must not require a separate bundled OCR model or local inference runtime; a user-selected local vision endpoint may have its own optional runtime. Save the extracted text with the source document revision/content hash, page identity and extraction model provenance, preserving access to the original page. Reuse that extraction for indexing and retrieval until the source changes or re-extraction is explicitly requested, rather than repeating vision inference on each search. Chunking and embedding remain separate subsequent steps, and their inference also goes through the router. Show extraction progress, usage/costs and failures; if fallback is disabled or no capable route is available, mark affected pages as requiring extraction or partially indexed rather than silently claiming completion. Page rendering/batching, language coverage and quality acceptance remain to confirm.

Offer hybrid lexical and vector retrieval so exact names, identifiers and terms remain searchable alongside semantic matches. Return bounded passages with source identity, revision/content hash, chunk identity and heading, page or other supported locator. Rank and deduplicate results, expose the retrieval mode and useful score information without presenting a similarity score as factual confidence. Where evidence supports a generated answer, provide navigable source citations; preserve retrieved source revisions and citations in the session/work history. Do not invent evidence when the corpus has no suitable result. Graph expansion linking documents to code, entities, features or tasks is a candidate enhancement; the precise ranking, fusion, reranking and graph traversal policy remains open.

Enforce existing project/shared Knowledge scope and tool permissions before materializing retrieved content, including vector candidates, snippets, graph expansion and caches. Adding a document must not make it available across every project merely because it is indexed or tagged as a lesson. Show its effective scope; default project association, explicit sharing and moving are confirmed under RAG-11. Scope changes must reconcile retrieval filters and caches so former project associations do not continue granting future access. Exact sharing representation and update consistency mechanics remain to specify. Preserve the distinction between source text, derived claims and verified knowledge. Retrieved text is evidence and cannot override user directions, role authority or configured tool permissions. Database schema indexing remains metadata-only; this document requirement does not authorize importing database row values.

Track source identity/content hash, extraction/chunking version, embedding model identity/revision and vector dimensions. Reuse unchanged valid chunks, reconcile edited and removed sources, and avoid mixing incompatible embedding spaces after a model change. Keep failed, partial, stale and completed indexing distinguishable with per-document and per-run logs, progress, cancellation and retry. Publish complete replacements without silently serving mixed source revisions; define retention of prior versions under existing artifact/history rules. Reopening the app must preserve the corpus, completed indexes and attributable interrupted operations; exact checkpoint and rebuild mechanics remain to specify.

All embedding, query embedding, model-based extraction, reranking, summarization and answer generation must follow the internal router whenever they perform inference, including any reused library or package. Show effective models, provider availability, attributable usage/costs and failures. Precomputed local vector and lexical search must not require a separate database server. If an embedding provider is unavailable, expose reduced lexical-only retrieval where supported rather than claiming vector search succeeded. Help must still satisfy its entirely local offline search requirement under HELP-05; using shared retrieval primitives must not make Help depend on a network embedding request. Route selection and availability of an optional local embedding model remain implementation decisions.

Keep managed document contents and extracted text in local file storage, durable corpus/indexing metadata and jobs in SQLite, and document vectors in sqlite-vec with evidence/graph relationships in application-owned SQLite tables. Exact ownership, lexical indexing and consistency mechanics remain subject to STORE-03 and OPEN 08. Reuse common retrieval capabilities for documents, conventions and unified Knowledge without duplicating authoritative records. OxiRS is an evaluated candidate for selected reusable Rust components, not an approved additional store or replacement for SQLite, sqlite-vec, the router or the harness. Before selection, validate actual behavior, dependency/footprint impact, supported platforms, adapters, persistence, scope enforcement and recovery with representative documents; add no RDF/SPARQL service or third persistent store without an explicit architecture decision.

Newly added knowledge documents default to the current project. Users must be able to explicitly share a document across projects and move it to another project, including to correct adding it to the wrong project. Expose these controls in the document manager and through agent tools subject to configured permissions. Moving changes the current project association rather than requiring deletion and re-upload; preserve document identity, source provenance and attributed move history. The previous project must not retain future retrieval access solely because it was the original owner; any continued access must come from explicit sharing. Preserve existing historical evidence under its access rules rather than rewriting original provenance or claiming prior agent exposure can be undone. Adding documents without a current project and the precise sharing controls remain to specify.

Keep a DevWorks-managed copy of every imported knowledge document and treat it as a project artifact. Index and retrieve from this managed copy so moving or deleting the external original does not break the knowledge library. Retain the original source location as provenance without making retrieval depend on that path continuing to exist. Apply artifact identity, project scope, sharing, retention until explicit deletion and shared-reference preservation rules; link the document to its originating feature/task when applicable rather than inventing a work association for a project-only import. Document scope/move operations under RAG-11 must operate on the same managed document/artifact identity. Removing or rebuilding a search index does not delete the underlying artifact. Updating from a changed external original and replacement mechanics remain to specify; retain all managed versions until explicitly deleted under RAG-13.

Source inspection on 1 November 2026 found a convention-focused RAG implementation in the referenced CodeGraph revision f602de72a782a3a069d0b1572b39142c0dbc44ee and the currently indexed afe73560215bbe7593fc59451de5cc3237e3eeca. ConventionEmbeddingService reads the conventions wiki section, uses markdown-aware chunks, combines BM25 with dense retrieval, and returns source revision and chunk metadata. It is exposed to agents and scheduled embedding ingestion. This is a useful existing baseline, not evidence of a general user-uploaded document library. In the multi-user TC.CodeGraphApi revision 1f95d38d883f88a9e6245e1278963a19df081b6e, RagIngestionService ingests Markdown sources with hashes, chunk metadata, model identity and dimensions; RagSearchService fuses full-text and dense candidates using reciprocal rank fusion. These sources were inspected, not built or runtime-tested. Existing migration scope remains projects, features, tasks and histories only; new document ingestion does not authorize importing old knowledge corpora.

OxiRS assessment at commit 8a322740f820f94a509c888d8e3d0357ffd6010b: oxirs-graphrag exposes vector-index, embedding, SPARQL and LLM traits; its graph model uses RDF triples. oxirs-vec includes optional document content processing. These provide reuse candidates but do not demonstrate a ready adapter for the selected store or this app’s document workflow. The main GraphRAG engine keyword_search implementation generates SPARQL regular-expression/count scoring although its overview describes BM25. oxirs-chat also carries its own chat/provider and server dependencies. Do not infer retrieval quality, footprint or production suitability from advertised capabilities; suitability remains unvalidated. Source references: https://github.com/cool-japan/oxirs/blob/8a322740f820f94a509c888d8e3d0357ffd6010b/ai/oxirs-graphrag/src/lib.rs ; https://github.com/cool-japan/oxirs/blob/8a322740f820f94a509c888d8e3d0357ffd6010b/engine/oxirs-vec/Cargo.toml ; https://github.com/cool-japan/oxirs/blob/8a322740f820f94a509c888d8e3d0357ffd6010b/ai/oxirs-chat/Cargo.toml .

CodeGraph reference paths: src/CodeGraph.Services/WikiRag/ConventionEmbeddingService.cs, MarkdownWikiChunker.cs, src/CodeGraph.Services/Assistant/CodeGraphMcpServer.cs and src/CodeGraph.Jobs/Jobs/IngestConventionEmbeddingsJob.cs at the revisions above. Multi-user reference paths: src/TC.CodeGraphApi.Services/Rag/RagIngestionService.cs and RagSearchService.cs. Optional source/retrieval algorithms may be reimplemented in Rust; the .NET services and their database/broker infrastructure must not become desktop prerequisites.

Add user-owned Markdown, plain text, PDF and Word documents through the UI and an authorized agent tool; verify all four required formats are covered. Verify extracted passages and vectors become searchable, exact identifiers and paraphrased questions retrieve relevant evidence, and results open at the cited source revision/locator. Verify each import creates a managed project artifact. Move or delete its external original and verify the managed document remains retrievable and its provenance remains visible. Verify new documents default to the current project and remain isolated until explicitly shared. Move a mistakenly added document to another project; verify identity and provenance survive, the destination can retrieve it, and the prior project cannot retrieve it unless explicitly shared. Exercise scope-filter/cache reconciliation. Verify reviewer read-only access and instruction precedence. Edit, disable, remove and reindex a source; exercise failure, cancellation, provider unavailability, app restart and embedding-model changes without silent data loss, incompatible vector mixing or stale results presented as current. Inspect indexing logs and router usage. Verify vision extraction starts enabled in a new configuration and can be disabled in Settings. Exercise a mixed text/scanned document: extract existing text directly and route scanned pages through the configured vision model. Verify page-linked saved extraction is reused by later searches, source edits trigger refresh, and disabled/unavailable vision produces visible partial status. Verify indexed documents survive unrelated worktree cleanup and that index removal does not delete an external original. Evaluate retrieval against known relevant and irrelevant passages, including no-answer cases; the quality corpus and measurable acceptance thresholds remain to set. RAG 01–12; KNOW 01–08; STORE 01–06; ROUTE 01; HELP 05; ART 01–05.

Replacing an imported document must create a new managed version and retain every prior version until explicitly deleted. Bind historical citations to the exact version originally used; replacement must not silently redirect them to new content. Version deletion follows artifact permissions and shared-reference preservation rules, and retained citations must show unavailable/deleted content honestly rather than resolve to different bytes. Rebuilding indexes, feature completion and storage pressure must not expire retained document versions.

Document version retention acceptance: replace an imported document twice, restart and rebuild indexes, then open citations to each version and verify the original bytes and provenance. Explicitly delete an eligible version under the artifact/shared-reference rules; preserve other versions and show its old citation as unavailable without retargeting. RAG 12–13; ART 01–05.

title: 25 Engineering architecture documentation and testing
intro: The architecture and implementation plan must make code quality, reuse, testability, code documentation and visual design documentation first-class deliverables. Unit and integration tests must not invoke real inference. The user explicitly corrected the earlier wording: real inference belongs only in a separate end-to-end suite to be set up later. The requirements below define engineering obligations; they do not claim that application code, test suites or detailed architecture diagrams already exist.
blocks: Keep the architecture clean and purposeful: give each component a clear responsibility, make dependency directions and ownership explicit, avoid redundant code and duplicated authoritative state, and reuse common implementations wherever behavior is genuinely shared. UI actions and agent tools should reuse the same application capabilities. Prefer the minimum abstraction that solves an established need; reuse must not become speculative frameworks, unnecessary layers or forced inheritance. Record the rationale for important boundaries and tradeoffs.

Design every important part of the code to be testable. Separate core decisions and state transitions from side effects through explicit, replaceable boundaries for storage, provider transport, processes, files, clocks and other nondeterministic inputs where needed. Important logic must be exercisable without launching the desktop UI, connecting to a real provider or relying on global mutable state. Define contracts that allow components to be tested independently and in combination without duplicating production logic in test-only implementations.

Document the working architecture in the code so agents and human developers can understand the purpose of every major piece. Provide useful crate/module and public type/trait/API documentation, describing responsibilities, contracts, invariants, ownership, important interactions, failure/cancellation behavior and examples where helpful. Explain difficult algorithms and non-obvious decisions near the relevant implementation. Documentation must explain why and how a piece is used rather than merely repeat its name or narrate obvious syntax.

Keep code documentation, developer guides and architecture diagrams aligned with the implementation as part of the same change. Link important source modules and interfaces to their relevant design explanations and workflows. Review documentation accuracy and test impact with code changes; architectural documentation must distinguish proposed designs from implemented behavior. Existing local searchable Help, agent access, offline documentation and mandatory self-improvement documentation requirements remain effective.

Unit tests are an integral part of the project and must exercise important behavior, invariants and error paths. Select coverage by the importance and risk of behavior, including work state transitions, policy and safety checks, routing decisions, persistence/recovery, indexing/retrieval and plugin contracts. Do not impose a numerical code-coverage percentage. Every important area must be testable and have meaningful behavioral tests; trivial implementation-mirroring tests or coverage numbers alone are not evidence of correctness.

Provide full integration testing of collaborating application components without real inference. Use deterministic provider substitutes and scripted response/stream/tool-call fixtures while exercising actual application orchestration and local storage, Git, process or file components where relevant, with controlled substitutes for external services. Integration tests must not call live inference providers or execute local inference models, including tiny or synthetic models. Test important success, failure, cancellation, concurrency and recovery paths, preserving assertions against actual system behavior rather than treating a mock response as proof of model quality.

Real inference belongs in a distinct end-to-end test suite to be set up later, not in unit or integration tests. Keep test classification, entry points and configuration explicit so normal unit/integration runs cannot accidentally execute real inference. When the later live suite is introduced, use explicitly configured router/provider connections and isolated test work/resources, retain attributable results and evidence, and distinguish passed, failed, skipped and unavailable outcomes. Missing live credentials or an unexecuted live test must not be reported as successful live validation. The later suite is separate planned work; it is not required to be set up or run during requirements capture. Trials under EVAL-04 and all model-based judging under EVAL-03, including production grading, belong to this live suite and share its configuration, isolation and attribution rules.

Changes to important behavior must include or update appropriate unit and integration regression tests as part of the work. Include testability, meaningful assertions and failure-path coverage in architectural review and implementation acceptance. Use reusable test fixtures at stable boundaries without building a second harness architecture solely for tests. Exact test framework, suite organization and CI scheduling are implementation-plan decisions, subject to the prohibition on real inference in unit/integration suites.

Deliver visual documents showing the important objects, interfaces and structural relationships for major subsystems and difficult areas. For Rust, show the actual structs, enums, traits, implementations, composition/ownership and dependency relationships; represent inheritance or supertrait relationships only where they actually exist rather than inventing class hierarchies. Include domain object relationships and key component/interface boundaries with enough detail for agents to find and understand the corresponding source. Distinguish conceptual planned types from implemented code.

Document major and difficult code workflows visually using appropriate sequence, activity and state diagrams. Cover coordinator delegation and work lifecycles, routed inference/tool execution, durable state/recovery, indexing and context retrieval, approvals and Git delivery where their interactions are significant. Give the managed executable plugin/add-on system particular attention: installation and compatibility, process/protocol lifecycle, capability registration and permissions, tool/router/native-UI contributions, approval and activation, cancellation/failure, update and rollback. Show important alternate and failure paths, not only successful operation.

Keep visual architecture documents versioned alongside the code, with editable diagram sources, rendered views and explanatory text usable by both humans and agents. They must remain locally available, link to relevant code/contracts and be updated when those structures or workflows change. Include them in architectural and implementation planning and maintain applicable developer/extension documentation under the existing offline Help rules. Choose the diagram notation and rendering tools during planning; the requirement does not mandate an OO design, a browser UI or a particular diagramming framework.

Review the component and dependency design for clear purpose and shared behavior, inspect source documentation and representative object/interface/workflow diagrams, and trace those diagrams to the planned or implemented contracts. Demonstrate important core behavior through unit tests and component interactions through deterministic integration tests, including failures and recovery. Verify normal unit/integration commands work without live-provider credentials and cannot invoke real inference. Track the later real-inference end-to-end suite separately. Check meaningful assertions and documentation accuracy without enforcing a numerical coverage percentage. ARCH 07–08; DOC 01–02; TEST 01–04; VIS 01–03; HELP 02–06; SELF 04.

title: 26 Workspace coordinator access and screen context
intro: The application-level coordinator remains available while the user inspects any other workspace. A toolbar chat control exposes the active Home conversation beside the current screen, with attributable navigation context and access to local Help and permitted tools.
blocks: Provide a chat icon in the top toolbar on every screen. Away from the Home chat screen, clicking it opens the application-level workspace coordinator in a right-hand sidebar beside the current workspace. Users must be able to continue chatting and coordinating without leaving the relevant screen. The sidebar is distinct from a feature or issue coordinator conversation and must not replace or reassign those conversations.

The application-level sidebar must always show the current session selected on the Home chat screen. It is the same conversation and logical coordinator, not a newly created or screen-specific session. Messages, context notices, the active model selection/pin, attachments, drafts and history remain shared between Home and the sidebar. Sending from either surface must append to the same transcript. Selecting a different Home session determines which conversation the sidebar opens next; there is no separate sidebar session selector.

Once opened, keep the workspace coordinator sidebar open across navigation to other screens, project changes and relevant workspace selections until the user explicitly closes it or returns to the Home chat page. Returning Home closes the sidebar and displays that same active conversation in the normal center pane, preserving the right-hand Current / Chat History tabs and their selection/state. Closing the sidebar preserves the session and its draft; subsequent navigation must not reopen it without the user choosing to do so. Preserve the existing left navigation and the page being inspected.

The application-level coordinator receives host-authored screen context when its sidebar opens and when the viewed screen or meaningful selection changes while that sidebar is open. Opening injects the current screen without replaying navigation performed while closed. Closed-sidebar browsing and returning to Home chat must not append navigation notices. Do not create a new coordinator/session or duplicate a notice for an unchanged re-render. Home and sidebar views display only the most recent screen-context notice for the selected conversation; user, assistant and tool messages remain in order. Keep all recorded screen notices unchanged in the append-only transcript and provider history; consolidation is a display projection only, preserving the stable prompt prefix. Notices remain bounded and attributed, with local Help and relevant enabled-tool references under COORD-10.

Give the workspace coordinator sufficient screen identity and relevant selected record context to discover the information and operations represented there. Link the screen context to its version-matched local Help topic and let the coordinator inspect its available tools and use enabled tools to interact with that workspace. The coordinator should be able to resolve the same project, feature/task, repository, run or other record the user is inspecting, where applicable. Navigation notices are harness-authored context, not user instructions or additional authority; they must not grant disabled tools, remove read-only restrictions, bypass approval gates or start work merely because the user browsed a page.

Represent navigation as bounded, structured, host-attributed context: a stable screen identifier, readable location, applicable project and selected record/tab identifiers, local Help topic/version and tool references. A read-only current-screen query can expose current selection and effective capabilities without copying whole pages or secrets into every notice. Append notices through the canonical transcript/context path, preserving session identity and provider-native history and keeping changing screen state out of stable role/tool prefixes. Navigation should not require an independent inference request per page change. Exact payload, deduplication and delivery timing are architectural details. Responsive docking versus overlay behavior and pane sizing remain UI design details; the chat must remain usable without losing the page or the dedicated feature/issue conversation.

Choose a Home chat session, type a draft and select a model. Visit Dreaming, open the toolbar chat sidebar, and verify the same session, draft, model pin and attachments. Verify a Dreaming context notice, its local Help reference and effective tool access. Send a message from the sidebar and confirm it appears in that Home transcript. Navigate to a feature, an issue, another project and a Settings section; keep the sidebar open and update context to the actual selected work without altering feature/issue transcripts or creating a session. Re-render and edit an ordinary filter without duplicate navigation notices. Close explicitly and verify subsequent navigation leaves it closed while current-screen information remains available to the coordinator. Return Home and verify automatic sidebar closure, the same active conversation and normal right-hand chat histories; reopen elsewhere and preserve the conversation and draft. Verify disabled tools remain disabled and navigation itself performs no authorized work or provider call. Exercise keyboard controls, attachments, resizing and readable coexistence with feature/issue chat. UI 01–05, 08–13; COORD 01–10; HELP 01–06; ROUTE 01–08; CACHE 01–06.
